questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My choice of MU was twofold. Firstly, I wanted to study at one of the world’s best law schools. Secondly, I have personal relations to Melbourne. An exchange semester was a great way to combine the two.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Generally my stay and semester has been great. The reason it is not a 10 is because I have been rather disappointed with the quality of teaching.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. MU is very informative. Don’t stress beforehand, as you eventually will receive all the information you need in due time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Loads of information emails and induction seminars.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It can be difficult and expensive. I was lucky to find something before I arrived.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be expensive if you want to live relatively central and close to the university. Otherwise expect long commuting times.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don’t know as I found housing myself.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration was relatively slow, and unclear in terms of if I had gotten the subjects I wanted. Furthermore, be aware that the subjects exchange students can choose are very limited, which was a surprise to me and a bit disappointing, as many of the subjects I find interesting were not available to exchange students.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop1 student service. But they can’t really do a whole lot, as exchange students are fairly limited in their options as just described.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful due to the limited selection of subjects available to exchange students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the limited availability of subjects and do your research beforehand with the university handbook, which is the MU course catalogue.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The reading material is mostly high academic level, but it varies a lot from subject to subject. The teaching however was not very advanced.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It compares as it is a mix of bigger lectures (no student interaction) and class teaching (based on student participation).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AI, Ethics and the Law
Public Trials
Human Rights Law and Practice
Global Human Rights Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Not really any of the courses I attended.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: None. I have been to Australia before and know the price level, which is very comparable to Copenhagen/Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: MU offers an abundance of student activities. Everything you can imagine, and most of it at very reasonable prices.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Whatever you are interested in. There are plenty of opportunities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the many neighbourhoods of Melbourne. Rent a car and drive to one of the many beautiful national parks not far from Melbourne.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Australians are very down to earth and easy to be around.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No, not really. Do as you would when you started at CPH university.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: MU is a very woke university.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality and humour.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Pack some warm clothes, lots of money and adjust your expectations to what subjects you are able to attend. Otherwise enjoy the amazing city of Melbourne and the wonderful country Australia.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately not the academics, which I had high hopes about. However, I have had some amazing experiences hiking and camping in the beautiful national parks.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I didn’t find anything particularly challenging. Maybe communication with family and friends in DK due to the time difference, but this wasn’t even really a problem.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go! You won’t regret it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
